title: L'Odissea di Cleopatra
canon: Per the Genesis Document (L'Odissea di Cleopatra_canon.md — there is no script; the canon IS the page): Cleopatra 'Cleo' Modica, 35, second-generation Sicilian-American social worker, divorced mother of two, lives in Brooklyn, New York — underpaid, overworked, strong family ties. Every time she sleeps her consciousness wakes in a parallel version of her own life — Modica in Sicily, Poland, Tokyo, Cairo, Moscow — fluent in each life's language, fighting to get home to her kids. The multiverse announces itself only through glitches in ordinary reality: deja vu, impossible events, time skips. All dimensions run on the same contemporary timeline.
look: Photorealistic contemporary naturalism — no sci-fi hardware anywhere; the multiverse reads only as quiet glitches. Found light only per the Light Law: sun through kitchen windows, sodium streetlamps, fluorescent tubes, winter sky, a hallway door left ajar — every source belongs to the location, mixed color temperatures and deep shadow welcome, nothing rigged. Fine film grain, muted print color, full-bleed widescreen frames, one locked Cleo face across every dimension.
note: Light Law pass 2026-07-18 — prompts from L'Odissea di Cleopatra_canon.md. Eight new moment-in-time frames (Marco's 2026-07-18 standard: human emotion IS the story — a touch, an embrace, a tear, a look held too long), none duplicating the twelve shots in specs/11-03-cleopatra.json. Carried forward from the 2026-07-16 spec: the one-face rule — every Cleo shot locks to 07-cleopatra-01-cleo-k2a.png (dark curly hair, olive skin, small cross necklace) — and the still-open ⚑ reigns-reset flag (00-series-overview's all-LA reset awaits Marco's ruling). NOTE FOR MARCO: the canon page places the home dimension in Brooklyn ('She lives in Brooklyn, New York'; Ep 9 convergence is 'centered on Brooklyn'), while the prior spec's home shots are LA per the syno logline. Per LIGHT-LAW §1 this pass follows the page — all home-dimension shots here are Brooklyn. Kuna, the grandmother, the teacher, Tokyo Joe and the children have no cast refs; prompts own them. Refs carried only when Cleo is in shot (she is in all eight).

stills.notes: Treatment, Episode 1 'The Awakening' ('Wakes back in Brooklyn, convinced it was a dream') + Concept Overview ('She is so excited to see her kids' / 'So she's starting to value her life a little more. You might too.'). The whole series in one embrace — a mother back from a life that erased her children, holding them like someone returned from the dead.
stills.prompt: The kitchen of a third-floor walk-up in Bensonhurst, Brooklyn, present day, seven in the morning. A 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair and a small cross necklace, in rumpled pajamas, is on her knees on the worn linoleum crushing her two children into her arms — a nine-year-old boy still holding his cereal spoon, a smaller girl with her arms locked around her mother's neck — her eyes shut hard, laughing and crying in the same breath, holding them like someone back from the dead. The only light is hard morning sun through the window over the sink, blowing out the lace curtain and raking across the cereal bowls on the table; the hallway behind them falls to darkness. Full-bleed widescreen frame, fine film grain, muted print color. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Treatment, Episode 1 'The Awakening': 'convinced it was a dream until she finds herself speaking fluent Sicilian with her grandmother.' The proof arrives not as spectacle but as a look held too long across a kitchen table — the moment the dream stops being deniable, told entirely in two women's faces.
stills.prompt: The back kitchen of an old family rowhouse in Bensonhurst, Brooklyn, present day, mid-morning. At a small table with a flowered oilcloth, an ancient Sicilian grandmother in a black housedress has stopped mid-pour, the stovetop espresso pot frozen in the air, her free hand gripping the wrist of her granddaughter — a 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair and a small cross necklace — who has just heard perfect Sicilian come out of her own mouth. The two women stare at each other, the look held too long, the coffee forgotten. Light is one bright window over the sink, hard on the grandmother's face, mixing with the greenish ceiling fixture; saints' cards on the refrigerator, the corners of the room going dark. Full-bleed widescreen frame, fine film grain, muted print color. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Concept Overview: 'She gets to a phone and calls the number. When she answers on the other side she hangs up, frightened. She's in two places at once.' The other self never appears — the horror lives entirely in her hand that cannot let go of the receiver and the hand over her mouth. Distinct beat from the old diner-two-selves shot (that is the seeing; this is the hearing).
stills.prompt: A wooden phone cubicle in an old post office hall in the Praga district of Warsaw, Poland, present day, winter dusk. A 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair, in a borrowed grey wool coat, has just set the receiver back on its hook and cannot let go of it — her other hand pressed flat over her mouth, eyes wide and wet, because the voice that answered in Brooklyn was her own. Light is the flat cold fluorescent tube above the cubicles mixing with the last blue winter daylight through the tall street windows and one warm counter lamp deep in the hall; her breath faintly visible in the unheated air. Worn brass fittings, an empty queue, nobody watching her. Full-bleed widescreen frame, fine film grain, muted print color. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Treatment, Episode 2 'The Teacher' ('Cleo returns to Brooklyn, seeks out her old teacher (Ezra's Brooklyn version)') + Concept Overview ('The way she cried when her mother dropped her off and the silly drawings he made with her to ease her pain'). Brooklyn-side of the drawings thread — the old spec's poland-drawings-reveal is the Warsaw reveal; this is the quirky first-grade teacher who kept one, and the touch across thirty years.
stills.prompt: The doorway of a first-grade classroom in an old public elementary school in Brooklyn, present day, late afternoon after dismissal. A 65-year-old teacher in a rumpled cardigan stands in the door holding up a child's yellowed crayon drawing kept thirty years — a white hill town in a six-year-old's hand — and before him a 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair and a small cross necklace has one hand over her heart, the fingertips of the other just touching the paper's edge, both of them still, his eyes shining at the grown woman who once cried when her mother dropped her off. Light is the classroom's fluorescent tubes spilling into a dark waxed corridor, cut by low sun through the windows behind him. Full-bleed widescreen frame, fine film grain, muted print color. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Treatment, Episode 2 'The Teacher': 'Episode ends with Cleo seeing Kuna watching her from across the street.' The Herald's first appearance in the still set — nothing happens, and that is the story: a child standing too still under a streetlamp, and a woman who understands she is being watched across dimensions. The look held IS the frame.
stills.prompt: A residential street of attached rowhouses in Bensonhurst, Brooklyn, present day, just after dark. In the foreground a 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair, in a denim jacket, has stopped dead on her stoop, a paper grocery bag slipping in her arms — across the street, perfectly still between two parked cars under the orange cone of a sodium streetlamp, a small dark-haired girl of about eight stands facing her, hands at her sides, simply watching. Neither moves; the look holds. All light belongs to the street: the sodium lamp, a corner deli's white spill down the sidewalk, warm windows in the rowhouses, the blue flicker of a television in one; the sky gone black above the rooflines. Full-bleed widescreen frame, fine film grain, muted print color. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Treatment, Episode 3 'The Ex-Factor and the New Equation': 'Cleo wakes in Tokyo, married to a version of Joe who's kind and supportive. She grapples with her feelings for this Joe vs. her ex-husband in Brooklyn.' The grappling in one picture — a tender kiss she permits and cannot return, one tear, her eyes already somewhere else. Human emotion is the whole story; no glitch needed.
stills.prompt: The small kitchen of a low-rise apartment in Koenji, Tokyo, present day, early morning. A dark-haired man in his late thirties in a t-shirt stands behind a seated 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair, pressing an unhurried kiss into her hair, his hand wrapped gently over hers on the table beside a bowl of rice and miso soup — and she is letting him, eyes open toward the balcony glass, one tear on her cheek, her face belonging to another life entirely. Light is soft grey morning daylight through the sliding balcony door and the laundry hung outside it, mixing with the warm paper-shaded pendant lamp over the table; the narrow hallway behind them falls dark. Full-bleed widescreen frame, fine film grain, muted print color. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Treatment, Episode 3 'The Ex-Factor and the New Equation': 'Gittes appears as a street artist, leaving a mural that triggers her memories of Tokyo.' The Trickster enters the set through his work, not his face — a woman alone before a wall, fingertips in wet paint, remembering a city she has only visited in her sleep. The mural depicts places, not words, so the no-text law holds.
stills.prompt: The handball-court wall of a playground in Bensonhurst, Brooklyn, present day, flat overcast noon. A fresh mural covers the concrete — a rainy crossing of glowing towers and dark umbrellas rendered in dripping aerosol color — and a 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair and a small cross necklace stands alone before it, fingertips pressed to the still-wet paint, paint on her fingers, her whole body gone still, caught by a city she has only seen in her sleep. Even white sky-light over everything, no shadows to hide in; chain-link fence, cracked wet asphalt, a dropped canvas tote at her feet, kids playing blurred and far behind her. Full-bleed widescreen frame, fine film grain, muted print color. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Treatment, Episode 10 'The Hero's Choice': 'She weighs her feelings for Kai against her responsibilities as a mother.' / 'She either chooses her kids or her new lover.' The weighing made physical — coat still on as if she meant to go somewhere, holding her sleeping daughter's hand instead. The end of the odyssey is a woman on a bedroom floor.
stills.prompt: A children's bedroom in a Bensonhurst, Brooklyn walk-up, present day, deep in the night. Between two narrow beds a 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair sits on the floor still wearing her coat, as if she had meant to go somewhere and could not — one hand holding her sleeping daughter's small hand, her forehead nearly resting against the mattress edge, a tear caught on her jaw, her son asleep an arm's length away with one foot out of the blanket. The only light is the warm spill from the hallway door standing ajar and thin cold streetlight through the blinds striping the blankets; the rest of the room falls to black. Full-bleed widescreen frame, fine film grain, muted print color. No text, no watermark.
